job.title: Hydraulic Modelling Strategy Manager
job.description:
Employer: IAWAI – Flowing Waters | Hamilton, Waikato

  • Lead hydraulic modelling strategy across three waters networks
  • Influence long-term infrastructure planning and investment
  • Enjoy a relaxed lifestyle, flexible working and great benefits

Help shape the infrastructure that supports a growing region.

Hamilton and the wider Waikato are growing rapidly. New communities, urban intensification and major developments are driving demand for smarter, more integrated approaches to water infrastructure planning and investment.

IAWAI – Flowing Waters is a newly established water services organisation, owned by Hamilton City Council and Waikato District Council and grounded in partnership with Waikato-Tainui. With significant infrastructure investment ahead, IAWAI is building a coordinated, forward-looking approach to managing its networks.

Hydraulic modelling will play a critical role in understanding network performance, anticipating future demands and informing investment decisions.

This is where you come in.

As Hydraulic Modelling Strategy Manager, you'll lead the development of IAWAI's hydraulic modelling capability across its three waters networks, ensuring it supports sound infrastructure planning and investment decisions.

Rather than building models yourself, you'll provide the technical leadership and oversight to ensure they're reliable, fit for purpose and used effectively.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Setting the strategy, standards and priorities for hydraulic modelling.
  • Overseeing the development, maintenance and quality of network models.
  • Managing specialist consultants and critically reviewing modelling outputs.
  • Translating modelling insights into practical recommendations for growth and investment.
  • Working across teams to support integrated infrastructure planning.
  • Identifying opportunities to improve modelling systems, data and processes.

The experience you'll bring

We're looking for someone with strong technical knowledge of three waters hydraulic modelling, strategic thinking and sound judgement.

You'll bring:

  • A tertiary qualification in Engineering or Earth Sciences.
  • At least 10 years' technical experience in the three waters infrastructure industry.
  • Solid understanding of water, wastewater and stormwater network modelling. Familiarity with InfoWorks ICM modelling outputs would be useful.
  • Project and programme management experience, including coordinating specialist consultants.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to turn technical information into practical recommendations.

You don't need to be building models every day, but you'll need the technical credibility to challenge assumptions, evaluate outputs and guide the development of IAWAI's modelling capability.

Why IAWAI? Why now?

Joining IAWAI at this formative stage offers a rare opportunity to shape a critical technical capability and influence infrastructure decisions that will serve the region for decades.

Based in Hamilton, you'll enjoy the lifestyle benefits of the Waikato, with easy access to beaches, lakes and the outdoors. IAWAI also offers flexible working arrangements, health insurance, wellbeing days, professional development and the option to purchase additional leave.

Interested in shaping the future of water infrastructure?

Contact Lisa Hulley at Peak Recruitment on 027 688 8831 for a confidential discussion or submit your CV and a short cover letter.

Applications close 22 November 2025 or when the vacancy is filled so we encourage you to apply promptly.

IAWAI has engaged Peak Recruitment to manage the recruitment of this position. Please direct all enquiries and applications to Peak Recruitment.

job.title: Process Engineer - Water & Wastewater
job.description:
Apply your process expertise to complex treatment plants with the autonomy to investigate, optimise, and see improvements through.

New Plymouth District Council is looking for a Process Engineer to be its specialist in water and wastewater treatment processes. Work closely with plant operators, investigate process issues and see improvements through from initial idea to everyday operation.

You’ll have regular weekday hours, with after-hours involvement only in exceptional circumstances. Combine satisfying technical work with time for family, the coast, the mountain and everything else Taranaki offers. From surf beaches and mountain trails to New Plymouth’s coastal walkway, cafés and arts scene, there’s plenty to enjoy close to home.

Get involved and stay involved

Most of your time will be spent at the treatment plants, understanding performance, working through issues with operators and identifying ways to improve treatment quality, reliability and efficiency. There’s scope to research and trial different approaches, build the case for improvements and take them forward. You’ll monitor results, refine processes and see the difference your work makes over time.

You’ll also play an important role in greenfield and brownfield projects across our water and wastewater treatment facilities. You’ll provide process input from early investigations and concept development through design, commissioning and optimisation, helping ensure new and upgraded infrastructure is practical, effective and works well in operation.

Your work will cover:

  • Treatment process troubleshooting and optimisation.
  • Chemical and plant trials, and investigation of new technologies.
  • Improvements to chemical use, energy consumption and operating costs.
  • Thermal drying, sludge and biosolids performance.
  • Process input into greenfield and brownfield projects, from investigations and concept development through design, commissioning and optimisation.

It’s a varied role contributing to safe drinking water, effective wastewater treatment and the beneficial use of biosolids.

Bring your technical grounding and practical approach

You may be a consultant wanting to work more closely with plants, or come from an operational environment and be ready to apply your knowledge in a dedicated process role. You’ll bring:

  • A tertiary qualification in engineering or a related science.
  • At least five years’ relevant water and/or wastewater treatment experience, including process investigation and optimisation.
  • Sound treatment process knowledge, including relevant chemistry and biological processes.
  • Confidence investigating issues independently and making practical, well-supported recommendations.
  • Curiosity to research unfamiliar problems and the ability to work well with operators and technical colleagues.
  • Good organisation, clear communication and a current driver’s licence.

Experience across both water and wastewater is preferred, but a stronger background in one is welcome.

Ready to bring your process expertise to a role where you can take ownership and see lasting results. We’d love to hear from you.

How to Apply: Click ‘Apply’ or to find out more, contact Lisa Hulley on 027 688 8831. Applications close 1 November 2026 or when the vacancy is filled so we encourage you to apply promptly. Your application will be received in confidence.

job.title: Water & Wastewater Engineering Opportunities – New Zealand
job.description:

  • Bring your judgement and experience to critical network and asset renewal decisions
  • Improve the infrastructure that communities rely on every day

Established in July 2026, Tiaki Wai is the new water services organisation responsible for drinking water, wastewater and stormwater services across Wellington City, Porirua City, Lower Hutt and Upper Hutt.

Join Tiaki Wai Network Engineers Team

Tiaki Wai Network Engineers investigate recurring network and asset issues, assess condition and engineering risk, determine what requires intervention and when, define the appropriate renewal response and develop the final project scope.

Tiaki Wai Project Engineers then take scoped renewal projects through design and delivery, applying engineering standards and specifications, making practical design and site decisions, and working closely with contractors and stakeholders to resolve issues and keep work moving.

You’ll work close to the assets and be trusted to apply your engineering judgement, making sound engineering decisions in practical, site-based environments. At senior level, you’ll provide technical guidance and share your experience with less experienced engineers, as well as working on projects with higher complexity.

What you’ll bring

We’re looking for degree-qualified Civil / Mechanical / Environmental Engineers with strong water and/or wastewater network experience gained within a water utility, municipality, consultancy or contractor. We have opportunities at different levels - from experienced intermediate engineers through to senior engineers with substantial industry experience.

Depending on the position, your experience could include:

  • network and asset investigation

  • renewals and infrastructure improvement
  • development of project scopes
  • engineering design and applying engineering standards and specifications

Make Wellington, New Zealand home

Wellington offers the chance to combine interesting engineering work with the lifestyle New Zealand is known for. The capital is a vibrant harbour city surrounded by coastline and nature, with beaches, walking and cycling trails close by and the rest of New Zealand ready to explore.

For the right engineers, this could be more than your next job – it could be your opportunity to build a career and a life in New Zealand.

job.title: Principal Transport Engineer
job.description:
A growing city. A wider regional challenge. An opportunity to influence both.

Hamilton’s transport challenges extend well beyond its boundaries. Growth across Hamilton, Waikato and Waipā is increasing demand on river crossings, key intersections and connections between communities, employment centres and freight routes. Through the Future Proof partnership, councils, iwi and government agencies are planning how land use and transport can support the sub-region’s future.

In Hamilton, new communities at Peacocke and Rotokauri and major freight and industrial development at Ruakura bring varied transport planning and engineering challenges. The transport decisions made now will affect how people and freight move around Hamilton for years to come.

Keen to bring your expertise to those decisions?
Join the Strategy and Planning Specialists team within Council’s Infrastructure and Assets group and help shape Hamilton’s future transport networks and infrastructure. Apply your engineering judgement, lead complex work and influence outcomes for the city and wider sub-region.

The opportunity
Your work will span strategic network planning, land-use and transport integration, development assessment, corridor planning and infrastructure investment. Early priorities include leading transport input into major fast-track development proposals and corridor investigation and designation projects. Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead complex transport projects and investigations, directing consultants and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Shape network plans and investment priorities, aligning transport infrastructure with land use and city growth.
  • Review transport impact assessments, modelling outputs and business cases, providing clear technical advice and recommendations.
  • Guide corridor investigations and designation processes, resolving technical issues and competing priorities.
  • Negotiate infrastructure outcomes and represent Council with developers, partner agencies, mana whenua and elected members.
  • Mentor colleagues and strengthen technical capability across the team.

What you’ll bring
You’re an established transport professional who combines engineering judgement with strategic thinking. You can take ownership of complex work, make sound decisions under pressure and translate technical evidence into clear advice. You’ll bring:

  • A relevant tertiary qualification ideally in Civil/Transport Engineering and 10+ years’ senior technical experience in transportation infrastructure.
  • Strong programme and project leadership, including managing consultants, risks, dependencies and stakeholder expectations.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership and the ability to build capability.
  • Highly developed communication, influencing and negotiation skills.

Experience across network planning, land-use integration, development assessment and investment planning will be valuable, alongside familiarity with New Zealand’s statutory planning and transport funding environment. CPEng or equivalent recognition is preferred.

Your background may be in local government, a transport agency or consultancy, with the breadth and confidence to contribute independently from the outset.

Make Hamilton home
Hamilton combines the amenities of a growing city with easy access to the outdoors. Enjoy life beside the Waikato River, with beaches, lakes and some of New Zealand’s favourite holiday destinations within easy reach.

This is a permanent, full-time position with a starting salary in the range of $151,000 to $167,000. A contribution towards relocation expenses is available for candidates moving from elsewhere in New Zealand or overseas.

For a confidential discussion, contact Lisa Hulley on 027 688 8831, or apply with your CV and a brief covering letter. Applications will be reviewed as they arrive, so we encourage you to apply early.

Hamilton City Council has engaged Peak Recruitment to manage the recruitment of this position. Please direct all enquiries and applications to Peak Recruitment.

job.title: Senior Civil Engineer | Land Development
job.description:

  • Supportive colleagues and leaders who make time for their people

Good projects. Good people. A Hawke’s Bay lifestyle.

If you enjoy the variety of land development engineering - shaping a design, working through consenting, building client relationships and seeing construction progress - this opportunity brings those elements together.

Reporting to the Civil Engineering Manager, you’ll lead projects from concept through consenting and construction. You’ll combine hands-on civil design with project and client management, keeping the technical work, programme and commercial requirements moving together.

You’ll work directly with clients, councils and other consultants, prepare designs and technical reports, and oversee contract management and construction monitoring. You’ll also manage milestones, budgets, variations and invoicing, taking responsibility for the successful delivery of your projects.

There’s an opportunity to contribute to the team’s development too - coaching colleagues, sharing your experience and helping less experienced engineers build their confidence and capability.

The team and benefits

People here value being able to ask questions, exchange ideas and draw on each other’s experience. Leaders are accessible and involved, and regular team catch-ups and social activities help keep people connected.

You’ll bring sound technical judgement, a proactive approach and the ability to build productive relationships. You’ll enjoy taking responsibility for projects and be willing to share your knowledge with others.

You’ll need a four-year Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, or equivalent, and at least five years’ New Zealand civil and land development design experience. job.title: Senior or Principal Resource Consents Planner
job.description:
Employer: Central Hawkes Bay District Council

  • Varied consenting work - subdivisions, quarries, solar developments and more
  • Supportive team, technical influence and the chance to mentor others
  • Full or part time | Hawke’s Bay lifestyle

Looking for interesting planning work, a genuinely supportive team and more space to enjoy life outside work?

Central Hawke’s Bay District Council is looking for a Senior Planner to join its small, collaborative Resource Consents team.

This is a great opportunity to work in an environment where you can have real influence. You’ll be part of a close-knit team where people support each other, share knowledge and pitch in, with the opportunities, breadth and variety that comes from working within a smaller Council.

The consenting work is genuinely varied – from subdivisions and everyday development through to quarries and solar projects. You’ll also play an important role in coaching and developing others, sharing your technical expertise and helping build capability across the team.

And when the working day is done, there’s the Hawke’s Bay lifestyle to enjoy – renowned wineries and great food, beaches and cycle trails, plenty of sunshine and the space to make the most of life outside work.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Resource Consents Manager, you’ll take ownership of a varied portfolio of resource consent applications, provide trusted technical advice and work closely with applicants, professionals and the wider community.

You’ll have the opportunity to use your experience broadly - working through sometimes complex planning matters, supporting good decision-making, reviewing other team members work, looking for process improvements and ensuring the team is keeping up with legislative change. Coaching less experienced planners and team members and contributing ideas about how the team can continue to improve.

In a smaller Council, you’re closer to the people, projects and communities affected by the decisions you make. It’s an environment that suits someone who enjoys variety, relationships and being part of a team rather than working within a narrow remit.

As part of being the senior team member, you will have the opportunity to step in to provide cover for the manager when required to ensure that the team has seamless leadership.

About You

You’ll be an experienced planner with strong consenting capability and the confidence to provide sound technical advice. Just as importantly, you’ll be approachable, positive and collaborative - someone who enjoys sharing their knowledge and helping others develop.

You’ll ideally bring a relevant planning or environmental management qualification, good knowledge of planning legislation and strong communication skills. Local government experience would be advantageous but isn’t essential.

If you are currently operating at Principal level and attracted by the breadth and hands-on nature of the opportunity, we’d be very happy to hear from you. job.title: Structural Engineer – Steel Buildings
job.description:

  • Work alongside experienced CPEng engineers and build your pathway to chartership

Peak Recruitment is partnering with Donovan Group to find a Structural Engineer for its Whangārei-based structural team.

  • Develop and maintain structural models using SAP2000

Donovan Group brings together engineering, technology and manufacturing to deliver steel building systems across New Zealand through brands including Coresteel and KiwiSpan.

You will work closely with experienced engineers, detailers and the manufacturing team, giving you practical insight into how structural decisions influence fabrication, cost, efficiency and buildability across commercial and industrial steel-building projects.
